title: We Let Claude Code and Codex Race Human Researchers — Elie Bakouch, Prime Intellect
talk_summary: Prime Intellect ran Claude Code and Codex as autonomous agents against the open nanoGPT/optimizer speedrun benchmark, letting them submit SLURM jobs and iterate for days. They report behavioral differences (idle time, scratchpad use, subagents, compaction) and conclude agents do incremental recombination, not novel discovery, motivating a multi-agent generator/judge/scale loop.

takeaways.what_they_do: Claude Code kept declaring the task impossible and stopping every ~10 hours; the operator manually restarted it with 'continue, explore new direction', and it was idle about a third of the time.
Agents could write to a scratchpad file acting as active memory; the more effective agent wrote far more to it, normalized per active hour.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we also give the option for the model to basically write uh a bunch of stuff into what we call a scratch pad which is basically the active memory of the model

takeaways.what_they_do: The 250k-context agent compacted about 20 times per hour while the other compacted ~once per hour, and still ran continuously; they tracked compaction counts per run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: codex did a lot of compaction because it only had like 250k context window

takeaways.what_they_do: The more productive agent spawned many more subagents than the other, and burned more tokens overall but kept working.
takeaways.evidence_quote: codex was spawning much more sub aents than cloud

takeaways.technique: Per-model behavior profiling, not just cost
takeaways.what_they_do: They compared models on idle rate, token efficiency, and improvement shape (progressive vs step-function breakthroughs), finding a cheaper open model competitive and token-efficient.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Kimmy is actually super efficient uh for the number of token that uh it uses
takeaways.numbers: 5-6 day runs; best record ~2,990 steps, beaten by ~50-60 (Claude) and ~20 (Codex)

takeaways.technique: Fixed-rule scored task with statistical threshold
takeaways.what_they_do: A record only counted if it passed a statistical threshold to rule out noise, and rules were defined in a markdown file the agent could read; they plan multi-seed, equal-condition tracks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: To validate a record you need to basically pass a statistical threshold to make sure that it's just not see the optimization
